sources.section: Build your own Front-end Framework / Library

summary.title: Build yourself a redux
summary.one_liner: You learn how Redux works by building a minimal working version from scratch: a reducer, a store with subscriptions, and a React Redux-style Provider and connect.
keywords: when to use redux vs component state
takeaways: Redux is a reducer function (state, action) => new state, plus a store that holds the state and notifies subscribers on dispatch.
Reducers must be pure and never mutate state; create shallow copies so unchanged objects keep their references and can skip re-rendering.
Keep state in the Redux store only when it must outlive a component or be shared; transient UI state can stay in component state.
Provider passes the store through React context, and connect maps store state and dispatch to component props.
summary.summary: The author, from Zapier, argues that Redux is best understood by implementing it. Starting with a plain JavaScript state object and a note-taking app, the article shows why unstructured global mutation becomes hard to debug and test. It then builds a reducer with immutable updates, a createStore function with dispatch, getState and subscribe, and a React container that wires the store to components. It finishes by implementing Provider and connect in the style of React Redux. The code uses older React APIs such as componentWillMount and legacy context.
